OH-2025-HB1020.s: The bill would temporarily suspend the motor fuel tax and make other changes to state law. It would also repeal rules on unclaimed funds, create an electric bill credit, and raise the homestead exemption amount and income limit for qualifying homeowners. The bill would make an appropriation and declare an emergency.
OH-2025-HB1020.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1021.s: Would name a portion of U.S. Route 42 in Greene County and Warren County as the Deputy Chris Longfellow Memorial Highway.
OH-2025-HB1021.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1022.s: The bill would change the rules for property tax refunds in Ohio. It would update several parts of state law that deal with how those refunds are handled. People who pay property taxes could be affected.
OH-2025-HB1022.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1023.s: Would create the Early Childhood Education Governance and Outcomes Task Force. A task force is a group set up to study an issue and make recommendations. It would focus on early childhood education in Ohio.
OH-2025-HB1023.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1024.s: This bill would change the Common Sense Initiative Office and the process for adopting and reviewing administrative rules. It would set up the office within the legislative branch, give it duties to review draft and existing rules that may affect businesses, and create a public comment system for those rules. It would also let the office review certain actions by licensing boards and commissions for possible antitrust issues.

OH-2025-HB1025.s: Would name the Long Rifle of Early Ohio as Ohio’s official state firearm.
OH-2025-HB1025.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1026.s: The bill would increase and expand Ohio’s research and development tax credit. It would change state tax law rules for this tax break for research and development costs.
OH-2025-HB1026.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1027.s: Requires certain standards for parole violation hearings. It would affect parole hearings in Ohio under the state law on parole violations.
OH-2025-HB1027.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1028.s: The bill would create the Early Childhood Opportunity and Enrollment Act in Ohio law, which would relate to early childhood education and school enrollment.
OH-2025-HB1028.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1029.s: The bill would change Ohio school law for chartered nonpublic schools that take part in the Educational Choice and Pilot Project scholarship programs. It would also set rules for school disciplinary record requirements. These changes would affect those schools and the school records they keep.
OH-2025-HB1029.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1030.s: It would update Ohio law on which credentials count for the TechCred Program and the Individual Microcredential Assistance Program. These are state programs that help people get job training and short-term credentials. The change would affect people and employers who use these programs.
OH-2025-HB1030.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1031.s: The bill would extend juvenile court and the Department of Youth Services' power over delinquent children from age 21 to age 25. It would also require the department to place felons under 25 in institutions within the department.
OH-2025-HB1031.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1032.s: The bill would set rules for how state agencies use artificial intelligence systems. It would also address AI use in labor and employment, including job and workplace matters. It affects state agencies, employers, and workers in those settings.
OH-2025-HB1032.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1033.s: The bill would prohibit unlawfully sharing a peace officer’s personal identifying information. It would affect peace officers and anyone who handles or shares that kind of information.
OH-2025-HB1033.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1034.s: The bill would allow autonomous vehicles to operate on public roads and highways in Ohio. It would change state road and traffic laws to add rules for these vehicles. It would affect people who use, own, or operate autonomous vehicles.
OH-2025-HB1034.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB1035.s: This bill would make an appropriation to support medical residents placed in family medicine or psychiatry slots. The money would be distributed to hospitals and used for graduate medical education residency slots in those fields. The Department of Health would set requirements for how the funds are distributed and used.

OH-2025-HB1036.s: This bill would create a nonrefundable tax credit for producing Ohio biodiesel and renewable diesel. The credit would be available to producers that meet the bill’s eligibility rules and apply to the director of development for a tax credit certificate. The credit amount would depend on the type of fuel and where it is produced, and the bill would cap total credits at ten million dollars per fiscal year.

OH-2025-HB1037.s: This bill would amend Ohio law to add 1 judgeship to the Licking County Court of Common Pleas. It would change the number of judges for Licking County from 4 to 5. This affects the court in Licking County and the election schedule for its judges.

OH-2025-HB1038.s: This bill would let the General Assembly rescind certain actions, orders, and rules from the Director of Health by adopting a concurrent resolution. It covers special or standing orders or rules to prevent contagious or infectious disease, and actions to control and suppress disease or illness, including contagious, infectious, epidemic, pandemic, or endemic conditions. If the General Assembly rescinds one, the department of health could not reissue it, or something substantially similar, for sixty calendar days unless the General Assembly authorizes it again.

OH-2025-HB1039.s: This bill would name the bridge connecting I-270 southbound to I-70 eastbound in Franklin County the "Specialist Nicolas E. Messmer Memorial Bridge." It would also allow the director of transportation to put up signs on the bridge or nearby approaches showing the new name.

OH-2025-HB105.s: The law changes Ohio rules for non-recourse litigation funding agreements, which are agreements that provide money for a lawsuit and are repaid only under certain case results. It adds new sections to state law and removes one old section. It took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB105.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB13.s: This measure designates November 5 as "Roy Rogers Day" in Ohio. It honors Roy Rogers, also known as the "King of the Cowboys," who was a singer and actor from Portsmouth, Ohio.

OH-2025-HB195.s: Updates Ohio’s Uniform Commercial Code, the state rules for many business and property deals. It affects businesses, lenders, and others who use these rules in Ohio. The changes take effect on 10/6/26.
OH-2025-HB195.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB20.s: The law makes it a crime to knowingly harass or block an emergency service responder who is doing a lawful duty. It also says higher penalties apply for threatening a probation officer. It was signed by the governor and took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB20.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB210.s: The bill would change Ohio law on the sale of used catalytic converters, which are parts in a vehicle's exhaust system. It would update several state laws and add two new sections to the code. The measure was signed by the governor and took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB210.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB251.s: The bill sets rules for how law enforcement can use drones, which are unmanned aircraft. It also adds some aviation facilities to Ohio’s aviation law. The bill was signed by the governor, and some parts take effect on October 6, 2026, while certain other parts take effect on October 6, 2030.
OH-2025-HB251.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB284.s: This bill would require iron and steel used on projects supported by state funds to be made in the United States. It would affect state-funded construction and other covered projects in Ohio. The bill passed.
OH-2025-HB284.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB291.s: Would create the Ohio International Trade Commission, a state panel to deal with international trade matters.
OH-2025-HB291.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB292.s: Ohio law creates the Ohio Defense Commission. The commission is meant to work on defense-related economic development and state finance matters. It took effect on July 7, 2026, with another part taking effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB292.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB297.s: Ohio HB 297 would increase the amount a county may give to military and veterans groups for Memorial Day expenses. It passed, was signed by the governor, and took effect on 10/6/26.
OH-2025-HB297.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB319.s: Would create a state law about the clinical teaching subsidy for Ohio state universities. It would affect how that subsidy is handled for those schools.
OH-2025-HB319.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB346.s: The bill would require people who must report child abuse or neglect to tell both a peace officer and the local public children services agency. It affects mandatory reporters and changes the state rules for child welfare reports.
OH-2025-HB346.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB433.s: Ohio law changes how amusement rides are grouped for annual inspection and reinspection fees. The change affects ride owners and operators who pay those fees. It became effective on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB433.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB455.s: This bill would change many Ohio laws on public schools and the Department of Education and Workforce. It would also remove a number of old education rules. The bill was signed by the governor and took effect on Oct. 9, 2026.
OH-2025-HB455.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB519.s: Ohio’s HB 519 would make it a crime to have an electronic device when the facts show a plan to steal a motor vehicle. It affects people carrying such devices in those situations. It was signed by the governor on October 1, 2026, and became effective that day, with some provisions effective December 30, 2026.
OH-2025-HB519.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB533.s: Ohio’s HB 533 would expand the kinds of vehicles that can be used in a vehicular homicide or vehicular assault case. It affects criminal cases involving deaths or injuries caused by driving. The bill was signed by the governor and took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB533.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB541.s: The bill designates a portion of U.S. Route 42 in Morrow County as the "Deputy Daniel "Weston" Sherrer Memorial Highway." It became law on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-HB541.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB611.s: The bill would change Ohio law to give cultivation and dispensary licenses to certain medical marijuana processors. It affects medical marijuana businesses that process cannabis in Ohio.
OH-2025-HB611.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB630.s: Passed legislation would change Ohio law on police escorts for farm equipment and vehicles that carry farm equipment and produce. It would affect farmers, drivers of those vehicles, and law enforcement officers who provide escorts.
OH-2025-HB630.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB654.s: Ohio lawmakers passed a bill that would raise the penalties for abuse of a corpse. It affects people charged or convicted under that crime.
OH-2025-HB654.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB692.s: Changes would be made to Ohio rules for household sewage treatment systems, which are systems that handle sewage from a home. The bill would affect homeowners and others covered by those rules.
OH-2025-HB692.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB733.s: Ohio HB 733 would add maple syrup and maple product production to the state laws that cover agriculture. It would apply to the parts of law that deal with farming, land use, food rules, and related business matters.
OH-2025-HB733.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB758.s: The bill would address sudden unexpected death in epilepsy, or SUDEP, by adding new rules on the topic in state law. It would also let a person with epilepsy join the Disability Database and have an epilepsy note on a driver’s license or state ID. These changes would affect people with epilepsy in Ohio.
OH-2025-HB758.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HB852.s: The bill would require a person appointed as a police chief to complete basic peace officer training. It would affect appointed chiefs of police in Ohio. The bill passed.
OH-2025-HB852.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HJR11.s: This resolution would ask Ohio voters to change the state constitution. It would lower the vote needed for the legislature to override a governor’s veto from three-fifths to a majority of elected members in each house. It also keeps the rules that let the governor approve, veto, or partially veto bills making appropriations of money.

OH-2025-HR544.s: The House adopted a resolution electing Sean M. Hutson to fill the vacant seat in the 66th House District. The vacancy was created by Sharon A. Ray’s resignation. It affects the membership of the Ohio House of Representatives.
OH-2025-HR544.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-HR547.s: The Ohio House adopted a resolution honoring Dahm Brothers Company, Inc. on its 100th anniversary. The measure recognizes the company as a family-owned roofing contractor founded in 1926 and notes its work for customers and the local community. It also asks that a copy of the resolution be sent to the company.

OH-2025-HR548.s: This resolution honors the Parma City School District for its 200th anniversary. It praises the district for its long service to the Parma, Parma Heights, and Seven Hills communities and for helping students learn and prepare for success. The House would also send a copy of the resolution to the school district.

OH-2025-HR549.s: This resolution honors Gilberg Furniture on its centennial and congratulates it on its One Hundredth Anniversary. It says the business was founded in 1926 and has been an important part of the New Bremen community. The resolution also salutes the company as a fine Ohio operation and directs the House Clerk to send it a copy.

OH-2025-HR550.s: This resolution honors the Mechanics Bank Main Office on its centennial. It says the office was established in 1926 and has served local communities with financial guidance and leadership, and it congratulates the office and wishes it continued success.

OH-2025-HR551.s: The Ohio House adopted a resolution honoring the Ohio University men’s club hockey team for winning the 2026 American Collegiate Hockey Association Division 1 National Championship. It also recognizes the team’s coaches and says a copy of the resolution will be sent to the team.

OH-2025-HR552.s: The House adopted a resolution congratulating Fierbaugh Farm on its 200th anniversary. It also asks that a copy be sent to the farm.

OH-2025-HR553.s: The House adopted a resolution honoring Leah Varga for winning a martial arts title at the 2026 ADCC Amateur World Championship in Kraków, Poland. It notes that she won a gold medal in women’s jiu jitsu in the girls 13-14 years, 55 kilogram bracket. A copy of the resolution would be sent to her.

OH-2025-HR555.s: The Ohio House adopted a resolution honoring Seville United Methodist Church on its 200th anniversary. It recognizes the church for its long history and its work in the community, including concerts, blood drives, and fundraising events. The House clerk is to send a certified copy of the resolution to the church.

OH-2025-HR556.s: This resolution honors Grady Short for winning the 2026 Division II state boys golf championship. It says he had a two-day total of 141 and played for Archbold High School. The House adopted the resolution and asked that a copy be sent to him.

OH-2025-HR557.s: The Ohio House adopted a resolution honoring the Niles McKinley High School marching band on its 100th anniversary. It also sends the band an official copy of the resolution. The measure is a formal statement of praise and good wishes.

OH-2025-HR558.s: The Ohio House adopted a resolution honoring the River View High School boys golf team for winning the 2026 Division II State Championship. It also recognizes the team and coach Chad Gress and says a copy will be sent to the team.

OH-2025-HR559.s: This resolution recognizes November 2026 as Ohio Military Family Appreciation Month. It honors military families for their service, sacrifice, and support during their loved ones’ military service. It also urges citizens to take part in related programs and activities and directs copies of the resolution to Ohio news media.

OH-2025-HR560.s: This resolution honors Emma Wagner and Saanvi Reddy for winning the 2026 Division I State Championship in girls doubles tennis. It says they are senior members of the Mason High School girls tennis team and recognizes their skill, perseverance, and sportsmanship. The House adopted the resolution and asked that a copy be sent to them.

OH-2025-HR561.s: This resolution commends the Canton Palace Theatre on its One Hundredth Anniversary. It says the theater has hosted films, concerts, theatrical productions, community performances, and special events since opening on November 22, 1926. It also says the House will send a copy of the resolution to the theater.

OH-2025-HR562.s: This resolution honors the Mason High School girls tennis team for winning the 2026 Ohio Tennis Coaches Association Division I State Championship. It also recognizes the team’s tenth consecutive title and sends a copy of the resolution to the team.

OH-2025-HR564.s: This resolution authorizes the House Chief Administrative Officer to pay travel allowances to certain House members. The allowance is based on each member’s round-trip mileage to and from the seat of government. It lists the members and their district numbers who are covered.

OH-2025-SB162.s: The law changes the deadline for health insurers to seek back money from health care providers. It took effect on October 7, 2026.
OH-2025-SB162.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB214.s: This bill would remove firearm mufflers and suppressors from the list of “dangerous ordnance” under Ohio law. It would also allow a person with a valid hunting license to use a suppressor on a hunting gun if the person is allowed to possess it under state and federal law and has registered it under federal law. The bill would change the rules for people who acquire, carry, use, or possess dangerous ordnance, including hunters and others covered by these sections.

OH-2025-SB276.s: The bill would have Ohio join an agreement with other states for school psychologists, which can help set shared rules for licensing. It affects school psychologists in Ohio. It was signed by the governor and took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-SB276.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB306.s: The bill would let insurers use electronic signatures to meet signature rules under Ohio law, including on documents sent to the Department of Insurance. It would also change rules for captive insurance companies and special purpose financial captive insurance companies. The bill would restrict repair facilities from requiring certain contracts tied to insurance policies, claims, title transfers, or legal fees, and it would require them to stop storage charges after a vehicle is declared a total loss and to allow insurers prompt access to inspect the vehicle.

OH-2025-SB315.s: Ohio would require the state SNAP program to start using chip-enabled EBT cards, which are benefit cards with a built-in chip for added security. The measure also makes an appropriation, or sets aside state money, for this change. It was signed by the governor and took effect on October 6, 2026.
OH-2025-SB315.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB459.s: The bill would exempt donated motor vehicles from Ohio’s casual sales limits, which are limits on occasional private sales. It would affect people who give away or donate vehicles. The measure was introduced and then sent to committee.
OH-2025-SB459.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB460.s: The bill would exempt required fencing around oil and gas well pads from property tax. It would affect oil and gas well pad sites and the fencing required around them.
OH-2025-SB460.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB462.s: The bill would create tax incentives for certain education partnerships between colleges or universities and private employers. It would affect higher education schools and businesses that take part in those partnerships. It also would change Ohio tax law to add these new rules.
OH-2025-SB462.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB465.s: The bill would update Ohio’s official map coordinate system to match the national spatial reference system, which is the standard way to measure and map locations. It would affect how state location data and mapping rules are set up in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB465.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB467.s: Would change when police must use a marked police car for traffic law enforcement in Ohio. It affects law enforcement officers and the rules they follow during traffic stops and other traffic enforcement.
OH-2025-SB467.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB468.s: The bill would require athletic facilities to install and keep automated external defibrillators, or AEDs, on site. AEDs are devices used to help treat a sudden heart problem. It would affect athletic facilities in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB468.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB469.s: The bill would set rules for the use of automated license plate readers, mass surveillance tools, and the data they collect. These are systems that can scan plates and gather watch-like data over time. It would affect agencies and other users of those systems in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB469.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB471.s: The bill would add two judges to the Franklin County Court of Common Pleas. The new judges would be elected in 2028. It affects the county court system in Franklin County.
OH-2025-SB471.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB473.s: The bill would designate September 25 as Dolly Parton Day in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB473.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB474.s: The bill would lower Ohio excise tax rates on beer made in the United States. It would affect beer producers and others who pay or collect that tax in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB474.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB475.s: The bill would temporarily lower some motor fuel taxes in Ohio and add a temporary retail tax on certain motor fuel. It would also require gas stations to give customers itemized receipts. The bill would set aside money to make up for lost fuel tax revenue and to make payments to gas stations, and it would declare an emergency.
OH-2025-SB475.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB476.s: This bill would make changes to Ohio laws that govern planned communities and condominiums, including rules for homeowner groups and housing properties.
OH-2025-SB476.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB477.s: The bill would change Ohio law on electric bicycles, low-speed micromobility devices, and electric personal assistive mobility devices. It would affect people who use these devices and others on the road, under the state traffic laws tied to them.
OH-2025-SB477.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB478.s: The bill would require voter approval before counties with more than 1 million people can levy certain sales and use taxes. It affects those large counties and the local taxes they may charge.
OH-2025-SB478.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB479.s: The bill would say that betting on elections counts as illegal gambling under Ohio law.
OH-2025-SB479.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB480.s: The bill would require a coroner to keep and store a DNA sample for later genetic testing when an autopsy is done and the cause of death cannot be found. It would apply to coroners in those cases.
OH-2025-SB480.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB481.s: Would designate October 8 as "Captain Eddie Rickenbacker Day" in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB481.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB482.s: Would designate April 23 as "Granville T. Woods Day" in Ohio.
OH-2025-SB482.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB483.s: The bill would name a portion of U.S. Route 68 in Clinton County the Captain Curtis Angst Memorial Highway.
OH-2025-SB483.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB484.s: The bill would change the judge of the Struthers Municipal Court from part-time to full-time. It affects that court’s judge and would amend Ohio law to make that change.
OH-2025-SB484.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SB485.s: This bill would change Ohio law on Medicare supplement policies, also called Medigap. It would require issuers that offer coverage to people 65 and older to offer the same coverage to people under 65 who are eligible for and enrolled in Medicare because of disability or end stage renal disease. The bill also says those policies could not exclude benefits for preexisting conditions, and the premiums for people 64 or younger could not be more than 125% of the premiums for people age 65. It would also let some younger Medicare enrollees apply for this coverage during a 180-day period after the new section takes effect.

OH-2025-SB486.s: The bill would name a portion of State Route 674 in Fairfield County and Pickaway County the "Captain Seth R. Koval Memorial Highway." It would also allow the director of transportation to put up markers along the highway showing that name.

OH-2025-SB487.s: This bill would add strangulation to the list of offenses that can be used to get a protection order. It would also increase the penalty for violating a protection order. The changes would affect people who seek protection orders and people who are under those orders.

OH-2025-SB488.s: This bill would make changes to Ohio’s laws for regulating cosmetologists and barbers. It would amend many sections of the Revised Code and repeal several others related to those professions. The bill also changes some section numbers in the law.

OH-2025-SB489.s: This bill would designate January as "Ohio Mentoring Month." It says the month is meant to emphasize the importance of mentorship in supporting personal growth, educational achievement, and professional development. It would also acknowledge people who dedicate their time and experience to guiding and supporting others.

OH-2025-SB490.s: This bill would designate May as Ohio Mental Health Awareness Month. It is meant to increase public awareness of mental health and encourage people to seek support. It would also recognize the professionals who provide mental health services.

OH-2025-SB491.s: This bill would create a new school funding system for public and chartered nonpublic schools. It would use a statewide per-pupil payment based on a single statewide property tax and a higher state sales tax, and it would repeal school district property and income taxes. It would also end the classroom facilities assistance programs, the Educational Choice and Pilot Project scholarship programs, and interdistrict open enrollment. Educational service centers would have to transport students on a countywide basis.

OH-2025-SB492.s: This bill would bar homeowners, neighborhood, civic, and other associations from blocking the display of certain flags and yard signs when they are shown under the law. It covers the United States flag, the state flag, the POW/MIA flag, and service flags for military family members. It would also bar these associations from restricting the gathering of signatures for candidacy papers and several kinds of petitions.

OH-2025-SCR21.s: A resolution is a formal statement by lawmakers. It would condemn the Russian Federation for taking children from Ukraine by force, moving them to other places, and then putting them up for illegal adoption and indoctrination. It affects the Russian Federation and children from Ukraine.
OH-2025-SCR21.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SR446.s: The Ohio Senate adopted a resolution honoring the YWCA of Alliance on its 100th anniversary. It recognizes the group’s work over the years, including transitional housing for women and families, child care, job training, and efforts for gender equality and racial justice. The Senate also directed that a copy of the resolution be sent to the YWCA of Alliance.

OH-2025-SR447.s: A resolution is a formal statement that recognizes the contributions of immigrants and refugees. It would also urge federal action to help address Ohio’s workforce shortages.
OH-2025-SR447.src: Ohio legislature, long title (via Open States)

OH-2025-SR448.s: The Senate adopted a resolution honoring the memory of Gerald L. Stebelton and offering condolences to his family and friends. It says he served in the Ohio House of Representatives, worked on the House Education Committee, and was active in local community and civic groups.

OH-2025-SR449.s: The Ohio Senate adopted a resolution recognizing Disability Employment Awareness Month in Ohio for October 2026. It also asks the Senate clerk to send copies of the resolution to Ohio news media. The measure is a formal statement of recognition, not a law that changes rules.

OH-2025-SR450.s: The Senate adopted a resolution honoring Matthew Dietrich for his retirement from the Ohio Rail Development Commission and for his service there. It also extends best wishes for his future and asks that a copy be sent to him.

OH-2025-SR451.s: The Ohio Senate adopted a resolution honoring Leah Varga for being named the 2026 ADCC Amateur World Champion and sent her an official copy of the resolution.

OH-2025-SR452.s: The Ohio Senate adopted a resolution honoring Julie Faust for her retirement from the Ohio Legislative Service Commission.

OH-2025-SR453.s: This resolution honors Mary Jo Harris for her service to the State of Ohio and recognizes her retirement from the Ohio Senate staff. It says she started in 1992 as a secretary, later served as executive assistant to the Senate President, and was named Rules and Reference Clerk. The Senate also directs the Clerk to send her a copy of the resolution.

OH-2025-SR454.s: The Ohio Senate adopted a resolution honoring Liz Connolly for her service to the state. It recognizes her retirement from the Ohio Senate staff after about 40 years of work, starting in 1986. The resolution also asks that a copy be sent to her.

OH-2025-SR455.s: The resolution honors the Canton Palace Theatre on its 100th anniversary and recognizes its long role in local arts and entertainment. It also notes the work of the people connected with the theater, including leaders, performers, crew, and volunteers. The Senate clerk would send a copy of the resolution to the theater.

OH-2025-SR456.s: This resolution honors International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers Local 212 on its One Hundred Twenty-fifth Anniversary. It says the group has served people in the electrical and telecommunications industries and has provided training, health care, safe working conditions, and protected wages and employment. It also congratulates the members and sends a copy of the resolution to the group.

OH-2025-SR457.s: This resolution honors Jodie Han for winning the 2026 Ohio High School Athletic Association Division I State Championship in girls golf. It recognizes her as a junior on the Olentangy High School girls golf team and says a copy of the resolution will be sent to her.

OH-2025-SR458.s: This resolution honors the River View High School boys golf team for winning the 2026 Division II State Championship. It also recognizes the team’s coaches and says a copy of the resolution will be sent to the team.
